text: David said to himself, "Now, one of these days, I will be swept away by Saul's hand. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in the territory of Israel, and I will slip out of his hand."

versions.text: David said to himself, "One of these days I will die at Saul's hand. The best thing I can do is escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel, and I will slip out of his reach."
versions.explanation: The opening עַתָּה ("now") is unrepresented, and אֶסָּפֶה carries the sense of being swept away or perishing. Adding the connective also gives the line a better spoken cadence. (Minor; the current wording is otherwise accurate.)

versions.text: David said to himself, "Now, one of these days, I will be swept away by Saul's hand.
versions.explanation: Roughly two thirds of the Hebrew verse is missing from the current text: אֵין־לִי טוֹב כִּי הִמָּלֵט אִמָּלֵט אֶל־אֶרֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּים ("there is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines"), וְנוֹאַשׁ מִמֶּנִּי שָׁאוּל לְבַקְשֵׁנִי עוֹד בְּכָל־גְּבוּל יִשְׂרָאֵל ("and Saul will despair of seeking me any longer in all the territory of Israel"), and וְנִמְלַטְתִּי מִיָּדוֹ ("and I will escape from his hand"). The restored wording follows the earlier revision while keeping the approved opening clause, and renders גְּבוּל as "territory" and מִיָּדוֹ as "his hand" to match the earlier "Saul's hand."

text: So David set out and crossed over, he and the six hundred men with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
David settled with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each with his household — David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's widow.
When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he searched for him no longer.
David said to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be given a place in one of the outlying towns, so I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"
That day Achish gave him Ziklag; and so Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
David lived in Philistine territory a year and four months.

David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites — for these were the peoples who from ancient times had inhabited the land stretching toward Shur as far as Egypt.
Whenever David attacked a region, he left neither man nor woman alive; he took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing, and then returned to Achish.
When Achish asked, "Where did you raid today?" David would answer, "Against the Negev of Judah," or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."

David would leave neither man nor woman alive to bring back to Gath, for he thought, "They might report on us and say, 'This is what David did.'" Such was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.

versions.text: David left neither man nor woman alive to be brought to Gath, for he thought, "They might inform on us and say, 'This is what David did.'" Such was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.
versions.explanation: The passive "to be brought to Gath" is ambiguous when read aloud and can sound as though the captives were brought by others; the Hebrew has David as the agent ("to bring to Gath"). The frequentative "would leave" also matches the ongoing custom described at the end of the verse and parallels verses 9-10.

text: So Achish trusted David, thinking, "He has made himself utterly detestable to his own people Israel; he will be my servant for life."
